clue.text: He drives out to have a drink with a farmer

parts.note: to sup is to drink, taking small mouthfuls
a planter is a farmer, especially one running a plantation

explanation.surface: Someone is evicted after sharing a drink with a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supplanter ousts and replaces another, forcing a rival from their position.

clue.text: Muse gazing at the night sky?

definitions.text: Muse gazing at the night sky?

parts.words: Muse gazing at the night sky?
parts.note: the Greek Muse whose domain is astronomy and the stars

explanation.surface: An inspirational figure staring up at the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the Muse of astronomy is the one who studies the heavens.

clue.text: A game operatic heroine

explanation.surface: A card game and a heroine of light opera.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the solitaire card game; the other is the title heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo card game shares its name with the milkmaid heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.

clue.text: Men's assets may be seen as a proper basis for taxation

indicators.note: the letters of the two words men's assets can be seen as something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's property could be the fair basis for a tax bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A valuation of property is what a tax charge is calculated from.

clue.text: No-one's to catch up — that would cause strain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I is one, and 's stands for is, giving IS
to net something is to catch it

explanation.surface: Nobody needs to catch up, since that would cause stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run NO + IS + NET into NOISNET backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension and strain both describe a stretched or stressed state.

clue.text: Spots not considered

explanation.surface: Pimples and a hasty decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots on the skin form an eruption; a hasty act is done without thinking.

clue.text: American way to transform fish

parts.note: to turn something into another thing is to transform it
the pike is a predatory freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A US method for changing a fish into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a toll road or motorway is called by this name.

clue.text: Gets agreed arrangement set aside

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of gets agreed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone obtains an agreed deal that is put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be separated or kept apart is what being isolated from others means.

clue.text: Charge a couple of hundred to operate

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them make CC
to use something is to operate it

explanation.surface: A fee of two hundred is levied for running something.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with a crime is to formally blame them for it.

clue.text: Getting little money, the working man is prejudiced

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny or pence, a small sum of British money
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A badly paid labourer turns out to be biased.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan view is one-sided, favouring a faction without fairness.

clue.text: A glass ship rigged fore-and-aft

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel and a sailing vessel described together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall sherry or beer glass shares its name with a sailing vessel carrying fore-and-aft sails on two or more masts.

clue.text: May set about the centre of Leeds or some other city

indicators.note: one word placed around a letter means it encloses that letter here

parts.note: may and can both express permission or possibility

indicators.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word Leeds is picked out

explanation.surface: Someone in May visits the heart of Leeds or another city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but is the verb, giving CAN; 'set about' puts the E from the middle of LEEDS inside it. Caen is a city in Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Caen is a Norman city in France, so it is a place other than Leeds.

clue.text: It's cold in the country — take a fur

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: China is a country
a chill is coldness

explanation.surface: It is freezing in a nation, so wear something furry.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent is prized as a fur.

clue.text: A way maternal care can be overwhelming

definitions.text: A way maternal care can be overwhelming

parts.words: A way maternal care can be overwhelming
parts.note: excessive motherly attention suffocates a child; the word also reads as S plus a word for maternal care

explanation.surface: Overprotective parenting can stifle a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocating attention is the overwhelming kind, and the word for it contains the word for motherly care.

clue.text: The reaper is an eight-footer!

explanation.surface: A farmworker gathering crops turns out to have eight legs.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a farm labourer gathering crops; the other is a long-legged arachnid, the daddy-longlegs, with eight legs.

clue.text: The whole unit is awfully green, it would appear

indicators.note: awfully signals that the letters of green and it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A complete item turns out to look dreadfully green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges GREEN with IT; 'is' and 'would appear' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number such as one, a unit, is the mathematical idea named here.

clue.text: Quietly coped with rising noise that could be provocative

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to have met a challenge is to have coped with it
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a ting is a light ringing noise

explanation.surface: Someone quietly handled a growing din that might be inflammatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enticing or alluring tempts, as anything provocative does.

clue.text: Offer conveyed beforehand?

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or beforehand
sent means conveyed or dispatched

explanation.surface: A gift that was delivered in advance?
explanation.walkthrough: The word read as two parts means sent ahead of time, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer something formally is to hand it over or give it.

clue.text: The musician's abrupt instruction

parts.note: a score's marking telling the player to make notes short and detached

explanation.surface: A musician is curtly told what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction telling the player to separate notes sharply, as if clipped.

clue.text: Keep giving notice

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on serving notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or festival is to honour it; to notice or remark on something is to perceive it.

clue.text: Go carefully through a list that may be opposed

parts.note: to comb is to search something thoroughly
a table is a list or chart of figures

explanation.surface: Someone checks a list for things that could be challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one can fight against or contest can be resisted.

clue.text: Against interrupting supporter if keen

indicators.note: one piece breaking into another means it sits inside it

parts.note: an aid is a helper or supporter
V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: An opponent breaks in on a backer if eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid and keen are synonyms meaning eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Urges simple reforms

indicators.note: reforms means the word simple is given a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone presses for straightforward changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or push someone forward is to urge them on.

clue.text: Scheme to raise interest

explanation.surface: A plot devised to stir curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a secret plot; to arouse curiosity or fascination is the other sense.

clue.text: Scots go for the company

explanation.surface: The Scottish word for leave, said of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots dialect the verb meaning to go is spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots verb for walk or go, and a band or crew of people.

clue.text: Strike young attendants and storms will result!

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
pages are boys who attend on nobles or at weddings

explanation.surface: Hitting the junior servants will cause an outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage violently about is to charge wildly through a place.

clue.text: The capital left over a fellow wanted

parts.note: on can mean over or on top of
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: The city is abandoned and a man is sought.
explanation.definitionFit: London is the capital city of the United Kingdom.

clue.text: "Who loves a garden loves a -too" (Cowper)

parts.words: Who loves a garden loves a -too
parts.note: a line from William Cowper's poem The Task with the glass building for plants missing

explanation.surface: A line of verse by the poet William Cowper with a word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowper's line pairs a garden with the glass building where tender plants are raised.
